abstract: TIGR-Tas system holds great promise for genome-engineering applications owing to its compact size and PAMless targeting capability. However, its low editing efficiency in mammalian cells severely limits its broader utility. Here, we engineered a highly active variant of ParTasR, termed eTasR, through structure-guided rational design of ParTasR combined with co-expression of the 3'[->]5' exonuclease TREX2. eTasR increased editing efficiency in mammalian cells from the original average 4.29% to 48.94% with an average 26.52-fold improvement, substantially outperforming the popular PAM-free version of nuclease-SpRY. Moreover, a single AAV delivery of eTasR in vivo effectively alleviates the disease phenotype of hereditary tyrosinemia type I (HT1) mouse model through targeted Hpd editing. Together, these findings establish eTasR as a compact, PAMless, and highly efficient genome editing tool with broad therapeutic and research applications.
